newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: S.LANKA STOCKS END UNMOVED, LOCALS SUPPORT VOLUME.
newsitem.headline: S.LANKA STOCKS END UNMOVED, LOCALS SUPPORT VOLUME.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks entered a phase of consolidation on Thursday and closed flat, but turnover was supported by broad domestic trading, brokers said.

The all share index closed 0.6 points lower at 856.5 with price declines outnumbering gains by 40 to 19. Aitken Spence rose 9.75 rupees to 200, John Keells Holdings 2.50 to 377.5, Hatton National Bank fell five to 290.

"The market is consolidating at current levels, from where renewed buying should take it up," said Aslem Ahmed of brokerage CDIC Sasoon Cumberbatch. Colombo stocks fell 13.2 points on profit-taking last week, after the all share rose over 70 points to 869.7 in July, brokers said.
Turnover was 123.7 million, led by across-the-board local buying, they said. Foreign buying amounted to 29.5 million rupees, while selling was 37.5 million.

Foreign inflows to Colombo stocks have eased in the last two weeks as overseas investors take a wait-and-see policy ahead of plantation public offers and the sale of debentures in the National Development Bank, brokers said.
The Public Enterprise Reform Commission said recently it would begin rolling out from September initial public offers of seven estates, in which 51 percent stakes were sold in 1996.
The commission also said 22.5 million convertible debentures in NDB will be sold later this month.
